chapter: Teaching, the 1951 Big Show and New York nights
title: Ray Nance jamming with Collins in the dressing room
summary: Ray Nance played violin with Collins until Nat's turn, and Duke never mentioned his absence.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Ray Nance was there, and Ray Nance would -- as you know, Nat would go on last. Right? Well, we have this big show with all these acts, and Ray Nance would come in the dressing room and play with me until we went on. He wouldn't play for anybody on the show but Nat.
He would actually sit in the dressing room and jam and play with me.

Violin. Until it was time for Nat to go on, and he would go on and play with us. And Duke, again never acknowledged his absence. It was just as if he'd been there all along. You know, he'd smile through it all. It never touched him. But this was -- as I say this was a very great band, and we travelled by train. And this is why a lot -- I would give Paul my guitar, and Paul would play some very pretty things on guitar. But I met Paul years ago when I was with Roy Eldridge in Taunton, I believe, Mass. He was up there with some little group, and this is when I first met him and knew he played guitar. But he was playing saxophone then but he also played guitar.
So I was aware of the fact, but few people knew that he played guitar.
He started playing saxophone, started studying saxophone in high school. (Inaudible).
